study type: Prospective comparative diagnostic study with outcome follow-up
exposure: Plasma glucose (PG) sampling methodology (traditional sodium fluoride (NaF) tubes vs. citrate-buffered tubes)
GDM diagnostic group (NaF-diagnosed GDM, additional citrate-diagnosed GDM, no GDM)
cohort: The study evaluated 578 pregnant women performing an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) between 24- and 28-weeks' gestation, with perinatal outcomes collected from a subset of 330 women who delivered in the hospital network.
finding: Using citrate-buffered tubes for PG sampling significantly increased GDM prevalence (27.5% vs. 11.9% with NaF tubes), and while NaF-diagnosed GDM was associated with higher incidences of LGA, cesarean, and preterm delivery, the additional citrate-diagnosed GDM group only showed a higher incidence of LGA compared to the no GDM group.
mod_finding: NaF-diagnosed GDM showed a higher incidence of cesarean delivery compared to no GDM.
gest_age: OGTT performed between 24- and 28-weeks' gestation (for mothers)
